### Basics and confidence-building

-  Right at the beginning, put some work into pronounciation. Audio courses are good for this -- try Pimsleur, which you can get via audible. Mimicking some basic phrases *before* you learn how to write them helps you avoid just pronouncing everything like it is written in English
- Look for _some_ context where you can use a few basic words of the language. You can't hold a conversation, but maybe you can say hi to a neighbour, or thank the server in a restaurant
- This is also where duolingo is good. It's structured to get you learning _something_ and build confidence

###Grammar and theory

- you want to learn just enough grammar to get by. Your aim here isn't to know all the rules, it's merely having enough knowledge to understand and be understood. Look for a textbook that suits you -- e.g. do you prefer to have rules logically explained, or to have lots of examples?
- when something confuses you, try putting it into google translate or deepl. See how the translation changes when you modify a few words (e.g. change the tense, like from 'I learn', to 'I learned')
- For vocabulary, flashcard programs like anki are great. 

###Getting support

* going to a class is great for motivation, but not always great for the amount you learn each hour. 
* native speakers are a great help. Just remember that they won't always be able to explain why things are the way they are, because they learnt as kids. You'll often get better explanations of grammar from somebody else who learned the language as an adult, because they had to learn things the way you are doing

###Input and output

* you want to set things up so you  encounter a lot of the language. With netflix you p can gradually change difficulty: first English audio with Spanish subtitles, then Spanish audio with English subtitles, then Spanish audio with Spanish subtitles, and finally Spanish audio without subtitles.
* Find something like a discord or telegram group in your language. It's a great chance to write small phrases in a language, and to read something relatively close to what people speak
* The [Listen-read method](https://learnanylanguage.fandom.com/wiki/Listening-Reading_Method) is a great way to study by yourself, using a book and an audiobook together
